test_title: RRB Group D Previous Year Paper (Held on: 14 Sept 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT about plaster of Paris?

options.text: It is used for setting fractured bones.
It is used in making cosmetics and casts for statues.
It is also known as calcium sulphate dihydrate.
It is used for making surfaces smooth before painting.

solution:
The correct answer is __**It is also known as calcium sulphate dihydrate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plaster of Paris is chemically known as calcium sulphate hemihydrate (CaSO₄·½H₂O), not calcium sulphate dihydrate.
 
• It is widely used in the medical field for setting fractured bones because it quickly sets and forms a hard, stable structure.
 
• Plaster of Paris is also utilized in the arts for making sculptures and casts due to its easy moldability.
 
• Another common use of Plaster of Paris is in preparing surfaces for painting, as it can be applied to create a smooth, even finish.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Plaster of Paris (POP)**

 
 
• Plaster of Paris is a quick-setting gypsum plaster consisting of a fine white powder (calcium sulfate hemihydrate), which hardens when moistened and allowed to dry.
 
• It is obtained by heating gypsum (calcium sulfate dihydrate) to about 150°C (300°F).
 
• When mixed with water, the powder forms a paste that liberates heat and then hardens into a solid, stable mass.
 
 
 
• **Calcium Sulphate Dihydrate (Gypsum)**
 
 
• Gypsum is a soft sulfate mineral composed of calcium sulfate dihydrate (CaSO₄·2H₂O).
 
• It is widely used as a fertilizer, in mold making for ceramics, and as a plaster material in construction.
 
• It naturally occurs in sedimentary rocks and is often found in large beds associated with other evaporite minerals.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Plaster of Paris**
 
 
• Medical applications: Used to form casts around broken bones to immobilize them during healing.
 
• Art: Utilized in creating sculptures, decorative items, and casts.
 
• Construction: Used to coat walls and ceilings before painting to achieve a smooth finish.
 
• Crafts: Employed in various DIY projects for making molds and small figures.
